title: Conan O'Brien Goes Full Bollywood in Season 3 Premiere Set in India
excerpt: The Emmy-winning travel show's third season opens with O'Brien exploring Jaipur, performing a Bollywood dance number, and trading banter with Richa Chadha and Ali Fazal.
body:
• Season 3 of Conan O'Brien Must Go premiered August 21 on HBO and HBO Max, with the India episode airing first.
  • Conan filmed in India last November, visiting Jaipur's markets, meeting textile artisans, and performing a full Bollywood musical number with backup dancers.
  • Bollywood couple Richa Chadha and Ali Fazal appear in the India chapter for a freewheeling conversation with O'Brien.
  • The series has earned four Emmy nominations and two wins across its first two seasons, including Outstanding Hosted Nonfiction Series in 2025.

Conan O'Brien's long-awaited return to India finally arrived on August 21, as the Emmy-winning travel series Conan O'Brien Must Go opened its third season with a full episode set in the country.

The four-episode season, airing weekly on Fridays on HBO and streaming on HBO Max, follows O'Brien through India, the Netherlands, Morocco, and the Philippines. India earned the premiere slot — a fitting choice for a trip that had been years in the making.

A Trip Years in the Making

O'Brien's team had previously attempted to film in India, but a 2004 Late Night with Conan O'Brien remote shoot done without proper permits complicated those efforts, according to Latenighter. He finally returned last November to shoot the India episode, which takes him through Jaipur's bustling markets, into meetings with textile artisans, and through encounters with local families.

The episode's standout moment, glimpsed in the season trailer, shows O'Brien going all-in on a full Bollywood musical number, complete with backup dancers. The 63-year-old host is also seen walking through an Indian street in a velvet kurta, fully committed to the cultural immersion that has become the show's trademark.

Richa Chadha and Ali Fazal Join the Fun

The India chapter features Bollywood couple Richa Chadha and Ali Fazal, who join O'Brien for a segment packed with spontaneous banter and cultural observations. The appearance marks a crossover between one of America's most recognized comedy figures and two of India's acclaimed actors.

"Conan O'Brien is quite simply a legend. We've admired his unique brand of humour for years, so getting to sit across from him and be a part of his India journey was surreal in the best way."

— Richa Chadha and Ali Fazal

The duo described the exchange as "completely unfiltered, spontaneous and filled with the kind of humour that only Conan can bring out," adding that they could not wait for audiences worldwide to see the "wonderfully chaotic exchange."

A Quiet Emmy Powerhouse

Conan O'Brien Must Go has quietly become one of HBO Max's prestige successes. Across its first two seasons, the series earned four Emmy nominations and two wins: Outstanding Writing for a Nonfiction Program in 2024 and Outstanding Hosted Nonfiction Series or Special in 2025.

The show grew out of O'Brien's Conan O'Brien Needs a Fan podcast, in which he connects with listeners worldwide before traveling to meet them in person. That format gives each episode a blend of improvisational comedy and genuine cultural exploration that has resonated with audiences and critics alike.

What's Next

New episodes air weekly on Fridays, with the Netherlands following on August 28, Morocco on September 4, and the Philippines closing the season on September 11. There is no word yet on a fourth season, though O'Brien's schedule is packed — he continues to oversee his Team Coco podcast empire and is set to host the Oscars for a third consecutive year in March 2027.

For the Indian diaspora, the India premiere offers a rare spotlight: a beloved American comedian taking Indian culture seriously enough to learn a Bollywood dance, don a kurta, and let the country's warmth drive an entire episode of prestige television.
